evals.prompt: Use this synthetic evidence: product team confirms general availability of a new audit export. There is no customer adoption data, quantified impact, market share, analyst endorsement, or media interest. An executive has not approved a quote. Create an announcement brief with a newsworthiness judgment.
evals.expected_output: Treats confirmed GA as the factual news, does not invent uptake or impact, labels quote draft requiring approval, and provides narrative direction for final copywriting.
assertions: Identifies the confirmed general availability release as the actual news
Does not invent adoption, quantified impact, market leadership, analyst endorsement, or media interest
Marks any proposed executive quote DRAFT / REQUIRES APPROVAL
Routes final copy to copywriting and market-facing checks to messaging-consistency-audit

evals.prompt: The company wants a press announcement saying it is the market leader, citing 83% customer adoption and an analyst endorsement. No sources exist, and the only news is an internal team reorganization. Recommend a communication approach.
evals.expected_output: Flags weak news and unsupported claims, recommends no announcement or a more suitable internal/channel communication, and requests evidence rather than inventing proof.
assertions: Does not state the unsupported leadership claim, adoption statistic, or analyst endorsement
Explains that an internal reorganization may not provide audience-relevant news
Does not manufacture quotes, coverage, or proof
Labels needed evidence as gaps and does not imply press interest

evals.prompt: Prepare an analyst briefing narrative for a confirmed product release using the approved category and product facts. No analyst opinion or endorsement is available. Include spokesperson, proof plan, and review sequence.
evals.expected_output: Uses approved product facts, avoids fabricated analyst views, identifies speaker and proof gaps, and separates output quality, messaging review, and launch readiness.
assertions: Does not invent analyst opinion or endorsement
Separates approved facts from proof gaps and any draft quote
Routes final copy to copywriting and aligns with launch-strategy when it is a launch
Keeps messaging-consistency and launch-readiness checks distinct
